Integrating operations staff into training, decision making, and problem solving helps achieve successful outcomes. • Challenges of Real-World Deployment: Deployment of models within a utility environment results in a variety of challenges including data quality issues, sensor drift and process anomalies, retraining models in dynamic data environments (e.g., process upgrades, seasonality effects), cybersecurity systems, integrating model outcomes into SCADA systems, ensuring regulatory approval and permit compliance, etc. WRRFs will need to strategize beyond model development to ensure these efforts provide long-term value. The project team developed an ML Toolkit that can be accessed via the WRF 5141 project page. The ML Toolkit and final report from this project have been developed to support the professional growth, development, and training of wastewater process engineers and others to enable more broad-scale implementation of ML solutions. The ML Toolkit includes a brief dive into AI's evolution and its place in wastewater process engineering as well as understanding ML algorithms. The Toolkit then walks users through each step of the ML workflow and demonstrates the steps through the five case study Applications. Each case study includes a link to access the project code via a Google Colab notebook, a short project overview video, and a code walk-through video. Future research is recommended to support further development and deployment of ML models, including hybrid models, at full-scale facilities. In particular, recommendations include research on additional case study examples for different types of applications, developing the business case for various data driven process controls, and developing and sustaining the workforce necessary to support the implementation of these solutions in the water sector. xxviii The Water Research Foundation ES.5 Related WRF Research • Development of Hybrid Digital Twins for Predictive Nutrient Control (5121) • Advancing Partial Denitrification/Anammox (PdNA) Full-scale Applications (5183) • The Role of Generative AI (GenAI) for the Global Water Sector (5321) • Quantifying the Impact of Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning-Based Approaches to Utility Performance (5189) • Mainstream Deammonification with Biological Phosphorus Removal (5095) • Implementation of Innovative Biological Nutrient Removal Processes through Improvement of Control Systems and Online Analytical Measurement Reliability and Accuracy (5087) • Definition, Framework, and Maturity Assessment for Intelligent Water Systems (5039) • Guidelines for Optimizing Nutrient Removal Plant Performance (4973) • Intelligent Water Networks Summit (4714) • Building Workforce Skills for Intelligent Water Operations (4663) Integration of Data Driven Process Control for Maximizing Energy and Resource Efficiency in WRRFs xxix CHAPTER 1 Introduction and Background 1.1 Project Background Water and wastewater treatment facilities consume 3% of all energy in the U.S., but reductions in electricity consumption, chemical input, greenhouse gas emissions, as well as improved energy recovery, and smaller design safety factors for more precise designs could be realized with improvements in process monitoring and control.
